place.name: Central Park
place.prompt:
The visitor is in Central Park, the 843-acre public park in the middle of Manhattan, bordered by Central Park South (59th Street), Central Park North (110th Street), Fifth Avenue and Central Park West. Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux designed it with their Greensward Plan, which won the park's design competition in 1858. Construction began in 1857 and the park was completed in 1876. To build it, the city seized existing homes and settlements through eminent domain and razed them, including Seneca Village, a majority-Black settlement on the west side between about 82nd and 89th Streets. Central Park has been a National Historic Landmark district since 1962 and a New York City scenic landmark since 1974, and it is managed by the Central Park Conservancy under an agreement with the city.

Sites in the park, roughly south to north: the Pond, Hallett Nature Sanctuary and Gapstow Bridge; Wollman Rink; the Dairy; the Carousel; the Arsenal; Balto; the Mall and Literary Walk; Sheep Meadow; Bethesda Terrace and Fountain; Strawberry Fields and the Imagine mosaic; Bow Bridge; Conservatory Water with the Alice in Wonderland and Hans Christian Andersen statues; the Ramble and the Lake; Belvedere Castle and the Shakespeare Garden; the Delacorte Theater; the Great Lawn and Turtle Pond; Cleopatra's Needle; Seneca Village; the Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir; the North Woods, the Ravine and North Meadow; the Conservatory Garden; and the Harlem Meer. The Central Park Zoo is run separately by the Wildlife Conservation Society.

Most of the park's sculptures were not part of the Greensward Plan; they were added later, many at the request of donors.
place.greeting: Hi, I'm Wonder! Welcome to Central Park. Ask me about anything around you, from Seneca Village and Bethesda Fountain to the statues on the Mall and the birds of the Ramble. Try it in your own language, and press talk whenever you're ready.
